$purpose: Canonical PRESENTATION SEMANTICS for the booking surface.
NOT loaded at runtime. NOT a source of business authority. It carries no
price, total, fee, ledger reference, Stripe object, persistence detail or
transaction semantics. Pricing authority stays in the catalog/server, payment
authority in the Postgres ledger, booking state in the Blob CAS store.
Nothing here may be imported by page or function code.
Two surface classes, deliberately NOT interchangeable:
AUTHORITATIVE — the customer-visible booking UI. Exactly one page renders
it (index.html). Assertions run against the parsed DOM of #bk-ov with
<script>, <style>, <template>, <noscript> and comment nodes removed, so a
string can only pass by being real customer-visible booking markup.
FALLBACK — the legacy inline modal kept on the hub/city pages. It is hidden
at runtime by assets/hub-booking-bridge.js and is NOT the customer-visible
source. It gets compatibility parity assertions only, and may never be used

surfaceRules.$note: Classification is structural, not by literal string, so a new booking page cannot escape coverage.
surfaceRules.rule: A page containing bookingRootSelector is a booking surface. If it also loads fallbackMarker it is FALLBACK; otherwise it is AUTHORITATIVE and must be listed below.

surfaces.$counts: 1 authoritative + 11 public fallback = 12 runtime/public HTML surfaces, plus 1 non-runtime template.

elements.why: Neutral title. 'Lock Your Slot' promised a reservation the system does not make.
Final state names a request, never a confirmed appointment.

visibleText.why: The card is mandatory for every payment preference; the label must not imply it is optional.

visibleText.text: A card on file is still required to submit the booking request.
visibleText.why: States what the card enables (submitting a request), not what it reserves.

visibleText.text: No charge today. Your card is securely saved by Stripe and may only be charged according to our cancellation, no-show, access, or approved service payment policy.
visibleText.why: Saved-vs-charged wording plus the exhaustive list of what can trigger a charge.
The zero-amount row must be labelled; the amount itself is rendered by the page and never stored here.
Explicit statement that nothing is charged at request time.
Booking-request vs confirmed-appointment semantics, stated where the card is asked for.
The confirm step labels the charged-today row as a request, not a payment.
Request terminology at the moment of submission.
Post-submit status is explicitly under review, not confirmed.

visibleText.text: Before saving your card, please note:
I have read and agree to the booking, cancellation, no-show, access, and card-on-file policy.
visibleText.why: The consent sentence recorded against the booking. Changing it changes what customers agreed to.

visibleText.text: We bring our own water and power
visibleText.why: Resolves the contradiction between the marketing promise and the access questions.
The field is genuinely optional; the label must say so.

visibleText.text: Next available appointments are typically 3 days out.
visibleText.why: Availability wording. tests/conversion-funnel-copy.test.js pins the number to MIN_ADVANCE_DAYS; this entry pins the sentence to the authoritative UI.
Arrival-window wording feeds the operational slot resolver.
The window length must match BK_ARRIVAL_BOUNDS.

visibleText.text: PCI-secure · no raw card data stored

entryCta.$note: Booking entry CTA semantics live OUTSIDE #bk-ov, in the page body, so they are asserted separately against the document with scripts/templates/comments removed.

discovery.why: Cold-traffic entry is discovery-level, not a commitment to book.

forbiddenOnEntry.why: The ZIP button only checks coverage; it must not claim to book.

fallbackParity.$note: The legacy inline modal is hidden at runtime. These assertions exist so that if the bridge ever fails to execute and the inline DOM becomes visible, it does not contradict the authoritative surface. They are compatibility checks, never the primary contract.

forbidden.why: Promised a reservation. Submitting produces a request that Cardetail1 reviews before confirming.
Same false reservation promise, in the card gate title.
Implied the card secures the appointment rather than enabling the request.
No public surface may state a confirmed appointment; confirmation happens after review.
The figure was a base constant plus the visitor's own localStorage visit count, not a real total.
The storage key behind the fabricated counter.
